title: Carpano Dry Vermouth
about: Carpano is where vermouth as a commercial drink begins. In 1786 Antonio Benedetto Carpano, working in a wine shop opposite the Royal Palace in Turin, combined herbs and spices with muscat wine, and King Vittorio Amedeo III adopted the result for the royal household. His nephew Giuseppe Bernardino turned the business into a vermouth and liquor factory at Piazza Castello in 1820. The Turin industrialist Silvio Turati bought it in 1939, and in 2001 it passed to Fratelli Branca, the Milan distillers who make Carpano today.

For more than two centuries Carpano was a house of sweet, red vermouth; Carpano Dry joined the range only in 2014, presented as the first new Carpano vermouth since 1786. It was built on the house’s traditional method with Branca’s experience in sourcing raw materials and input from Luca Gardini, a multiple world sommelier champion. Selected Italian wines are aromatised with wormwood grown in Italy and gathered in mountain areas, and with dittany of Crete, which gives the vermouth its savoury edge. It is drier and lower in sugar than Carpano’s other vermouths, bottled at 18%.

It pours clear and bright, almost platinum. The nose brings candied fruit, coriander, a breath of incense and lemon oil; the palate starts winey and slightly tart, then finishes fresh and balsamic, with citrus and green apple. Its natural home is the Dry Martini, where it supports rather than covers the gin; Carpano’s own suggestion is a Gibson of 6 cl gin to 1 cl Carpano Dry.
